title: Measuring Deep Learning Performance - An Empirical Study of Performance Distributions Across Architectures and Tasks
abstract: arXiv:2610.38037v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Context: Non-determinism in deep learning algorithm design and implementation leads to performance variation, meaning model performance is not a single value, but rather a distribution. These model performance distributions are underexplored despite their impact on robustness. Objective: We investigate the robustness of deep learning performance to sources of non-determinism, specifically focusing on how performance distributions differ across various architectures and tasks. Method: We conducted 186 experiments on image classification and time series forecasting architectures. Each experiment was run 100 times with different random seeds to generate performance distributions, resulting in 18,600 runs. Robustness was quantified using metrics for spread, symmetry, and tail risk. Results: Performance distributions are frequently non-Gaussian, particularly in time series forecasting. Model size does not systematically affect robustness --

translated_title: 测量深度学习性能——跨架构与任务的性能分布实证研究
translated_abstract: 背景：深度学习算法设计与实现中的非确定性会导致性能变化，这意味着模型性能不是一个单一数值，而是一个分布。尽管这些模型性能分布对鲁棒性有重要影响，但此前对其研究不足。目标：我们研究了深度学习性能对各类非确定性来源的鲁棒性，特别关注性能分布在不同架构和任务之间的差异。方法：我们在图像分类和时间序列预测架构上开展了186项实验。每项实验使用不同的随机种子运行100次以生成性能分布，共计18,600次运行。鲁棒性通过离散度、对称性和尾部风险等指标进行量化。结果：性能分布经常呈非高斯分布，尤其是在时间序列预测任务中。模型大小不会系统性地影响鲁棒性——
tldr: 该论文通过对186项实验、共18,600次运行的大规模实证研究发现，深度学习模型性能分布常呈非高斯分布（尤其在时间序列预测任务中），且模型大小并不会系统性地影响性能鲁棒性。
en_tdlr: Through a large-scale empirical study of 186 experiments with 18,600 runs, this paper reveals that deep learning performance distributions are frequently non-Gaussian (especially in time series forecasting), and that model size does not systematically affect performance robustness.
